Package arcade.potts.agent.module

Class PottsModuleFlyStemProliferation

java.lang.Object
arcade.potts.agent.module.PottsModule
arcade.potts.agent.module.PottsModuleProliferation
arcade.potts.agent.module.PottsModuleProliferationVolumeBasedDivision
arcade.potts.agent.module.PottsModuleFlyStemProliferation
All Implemented Interfaces:
Module
public class PottsModuleFlyStemProliferation extends PottsModuleProliferationVolumeBasedDivision
Implementation of PottsModuleProliferationVolumeBasedDivision for fly stem agents. Each division produces two daughters: one stem cell and one that is either stem or GMC depending on division geometry and rules. This module determines the division plane (affecting morphology) and assigns daughter cell identity.

    • populationCriticalVolume

      final double populationCriticalVolume
      Population-level baseline critical volume in voxels, read from the population CRITICAL_VOLUME parameter. Used as the fixed V_ref denominator in volume-based growth-rate scaling, so V_ref stays anchored to the WT equilibrium regardless of per-cell critical volumes — which matters when VOLUME_BASED_CRITICAL_VOLUME=1 causes daughter critVols to shrink below the population baseline.

    • wtDivisionSplitOffsetPercentY

      final int wtDivisionSplitOffsetPercentY
      Y-axis split offset (%) used for WT-style divisions, for any cell type. Defaults to StemType.WT.splitOffsetPercentY (93), giving the normal 93/7 NB/GMC asymmetry. Set to 50 in a setup file (WT or MUDMUT) to give WT-style divisions a symmetric 50/50 volume split.

      This applies wherever the WT division path is taken, including for MUDMUT cells dividing within MUDMUT_WT_DIVISION_ANGLE_THRESHOLD. The StemType offsets still apply to the MUD division plane.

    • gmcCriticalVolumeOverride

      final double gmcCriticalVolumeOverride
      Fixed GMC daughter critical volume override (voxels, after DS^-3 conversion). When greater than zero and VOLUME_BASED_CRITICAL_VOLUME=0, this replaces the formula-derived value in calculateGMCDaughterCellCriticalVolume(arcade.potts.env.location.PottsLocation), allowing GMC (and therefore neuron) size to be set independently of the division offset. Zero disables the override. Ignored entirely when VOLUME_BASED_CRITICAL_VOLUME=1, where critVol comes from the daughter's birth volume.

    • apicalAxisReorientationDistribution

      final Distribution apicalAxisReorientationDistribution
      Distribution of the angle (degrees) the NB's apical (polarity) axis is rotated by at the start of each of its divisions, before the division plane is chosen. The rotated axis is stored on the cell, so reorientations accumulate across a cell's divisions: a nonzero mean gives persistent turning, a zero mean a random walk. The division plane is then the updated apical axis rotated by a draw from splitDirectionDistribution, which does not accumulate.

    • lastSplitOffsetPercentY

      double lastSplitOffsetPercentY
      Y split offset (%) used by the most recent call to chooseDivisionPlane(arcade.potts.agent.cell.PottsCellFlyStem). Under the threshold ruleset this is always wtDivisionSplitOffsetPercentY; under linear_ramp it is the ramped value for that division. Read by the critical volume calculations so the split geometry and the resulting thresholds agree within one division.

    • divOffsetRuleset

      final PottsModuleFlyStemProliferation.DivOffsetRuleset divOffsetRuleset
      Ruleset determining the Y split offset for a division. Either threshold (fixed offset, with the 75-degree MUDMUT flip to the MUD plane), linear_ramp (offset ramps from the WT offset toward divOffsetRampMinPercentY as the drawn division angle moves away from the distribution mean), or switch_ramp (logistic transition centered on divOffsetSwitchCenterAngle).

    • updateVolumeBasedGrowthRate

      public void updateVolumeBasedGrowthRate(Simulation sim)
      Updates growth rate based on cell volume relative to a reference volume.

      Growth is regulated by comparing this cell's volume to an equilibrium reference. The difference is passed to the volume-based growth function, which adjusts growth rate relative to the equilibrium volume.

      Parameters:
      sim - the simulation

    • computeEquilibriumVolume

      double computeEquilibriumVolume()
      Computes the expected average NB volume from structural parameters, using a rectangular approximation for the post-division volume retained by the NB.

      For a NB growing at constant rate, the time-averaged volume over one cell cycle equals the arithmetic midpoint between birth volume and division volume: 

         V_ref = (V_birth + V_div) / 2
         = sizeTarget * populationCriticalVolume * (f_retain + 1) / 2
      where f_retain = WT_DIVISION_SPLIT_OFFSET_PERCENT_Y / 100 approximates the fraction of the pre-division volume retained by the NB after asymmetric division. The WT offset is used for every cell type, since MUDMUT cells also divide by WT rules within MUDMUT_WT_DIVISION_ANGLE_THRESHOLD.

      This reference volume is used as the normalization denominator in the volume-based growth rate formula, ensuring that at the average NB volume the effective growth rate equals cellGrowthRateBase.

      The population CRITICAL_VOLUME is used rather than this cell's own critical volume, so V_ref stays anchored to the WT equilibrium. Under VOLUME_BASED_CRITICAL_VOLUME=1 a daughter's critVol tracks its birth volume and can drift well below the population baseline; using it here would move the reference along with the cell and defeat the regulation.

      f_retain is wtDivisionSplitOffsetPercentY for every offset ruleset, not just threshold. Under a ramp the per-division offset varies, but every ruleset is required to satisfy the same WT calibration, which pins the WT mean offset at the imposed value — a switch ramp that passes the calibration gate has a WT mean within 0.3% of 93. A V_ref that tracked the ruleset's own offset distribution would let the growth setpoint drift with the very quantity the calibration fixes, which defeats the purpose of a reference.

      Returns:
      the expected average NB volume

    • updateGrowthRateBasedOnOtherNBs

      protected void updateGrowthRateBasedOnOtherNBs(Simulation sim)
      Updates the neuroblast (NB) contact-dependent growth rate.

      Growth is repressed by contact with neighboring NBs (local coupling) using a Hill function: 

           growthRate = baseGrowthRate * K^n / (K^n + N^n)

      Here N is the number of distinct NBs adjacent to this cell (see countNBNeighbors(arcade.core.sim.Simulation)), K is nbContactHalfMax, the neighbor count giving 50% repression, and n is nbContactHillN, the Hill exponent controlling how steeply growth falls off. When K = 0, growth is unrepressed if N = 0 and fully repressed otherwise.

      Parameters:
      sim - the simulation

    • chooseDivisionPlane

      protected Plane chooseDivisionPlane(PottsCellFlyStem flyStemCell)
      Chooses the division plane for this fly stem cell based on the offset ruleset and whether the cell is WT or MUDMUT.

      A rotation offset is drawn from splitDirectionDistribution. Under the ramped offset rulesets (linear_ramp, switch_ramp), the plane is built from that offset for both WT and MUDMUT cells, with the split offset from computeSplitOffsetPercentY(double). Under threshold, a WT cell always divides along the WT plane, and a MUDMUT cell divides along the WT plane if the drawn offset is within MUDMUT_WT_DIVISION_ANGLE_THRESHOLD degrees of the distribution mean, and along the MUD plane otherwise.

      Parameters:
      flyStemCell - the stem cell this module is attached to
      Returns:
      the plane along which this cell should divide

    • computeSplitOffsetPercentY

      double computeSplitOffsetPercentY(double rotationOffset)
      Computes the Y split offset for a division from the drawn rotation offset.

      Under the linear_ramp ruleset the offset falls linearly from wtDivisionSplitOffsetPercentY toward divOffsetRampMinPercentY as the drawn angle moves away from the division distribution mean, reaching the minimum at divOffsetRampSaturationAngle and clamping beyond it.

      Under the switch_ramp ruleset the offset follows a logistic in the same deviation, centred on divOffsetSwitchCenterAngle with width divOffsetSwitchWidth. It is flat near the distribution mean, so typical divisions keep the calibrated asymmetry and only extreme angles approach a symmetric split; as the width approaches zero it converges on the threshold ruleset. A linear ramp is flat nowhere, which shifts the mean split for every division and breaks the WT calibration — see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-graded-division-offset.md.

      Parameters:
      rotationOffset - the angle drawn from the division rotation distribution
      Returns:
      the Y split offset percentage for this division

    • buildDivisionPlane

      public Plane buildDivisionPlane(PottsCellFlyStem cell, Vector referenceVector, double rotationOffset, double splitOffsetPercentY)
      Builds a division plane from an explicit reference vector, rotation, and split offset.

      Genotype-neutral: the two canonical divisions are corners of this function, defined by the PottsCellFlyStem.StemType entries. WT(50, 93, 0) gives rotation 0 and offset 93; MUDMUT(50, 50, -90) gives rotation -90 and offset 50. The linear_ramp ruleset interpolates between those corners as the drawn angle grows.

      Parameters:
      cell - the PottsCellFlyStem to build the plane for
      referenceVector - the vector the rotation is measured from
      rotationOffset - the angle to rotate the reference vector by

    • daughterStemRuleBasedDifferentiation

      private boolean daughterStemRuleBasedDifferentiation(PottsLocation loc1, PottsLocation loc2)
      Determines whether the daughter cell should be a neuroblast or a GMC according to the symmetric division ruleset specified in the parameters and the morphologies of the daughter cell locations.

      Applies to both stem types. Whether a WT cell can produce a symmetric NB-NB division is controlled by HAS_DETERMINISTIC_DIFFERENTIATION: under TRUE the deterministic path is used instead and a WT daughter is never a stem cell; under FALSE a WT cell uses the same symmetricDivisionRuleset as MUDMUT, so a sufficiently symmetric division yields two neuroblasts. Setting the relevant threshold near zero suppresses that in practice while leaving the mechanism available.

      Parameters:
      loc1 - one cell location post division
      loc2 - the other cell location post division
      Returns:
      whether or not the daughter cell should be a stem cell

    • isSizeSymmetric

      private boolean isSizeSymmetric(PottsLocation loc1, PottsLocation loc2)
      Whether a division is symmetric by size: the larger daughter's share of the combined volume is below equalityOffsetPercentY. Relative, so the parent's volume cancels and one threshold serves every condition.
      Parameters:

      Returns:
      true if both daughters should remain neuroblasts

    • makeDaughterStemCell

      void makeDaughterStemCell(PottsLocation daughterLoc, Simulation sim, Potts potts, ec.util.MersenneTwisterFast random)
      Makes a daughter NB cell.

      Under VOLUME_BASED_CRITICAL_VOLUME=1 each cell takes its own birth volume as its critical volume: the parent the volume it retained, the daughter the volume it received. Both are floored at NB_CRITICAL_VOLUME_FLOOR_FRACTION of the population critical volume.

      sim - the simulation
      potts - the potts instance for this simulation
      random - the random number generator

    • calculateGMCDaughterCellCriticalVolume

      protected double calculateGMCDaughterCellCriticalVolume(PottsLocation gmcLoc)
      Calculates the critical volume of a GMC daughter cell.

      Under VOLUME_BASED_CRITICAL_VOLUME=1 the value comes from the daughter's birth volume, floored at GMC_CRITICAL_VOLUME_FLOOR_FRACTION of the parent's initial size. Otherwise it is derived from the parent's critical volume and the WT split offset unless GMC_CRITICAL_VOLUME_OVERRIDE is greater than zero, in which case that fixed value is used instead. The override lets GMC (and therefore neuron) size be set independently of the division offset, and is ignored when VOLUME_BASED_CRITICAL_VOLUME=1.

      Parameters:
      gmcLoc - the location of the GMC daughter cell
      Returns:
      the critical volume of the GMC daughter cell
